The Falcon Web Framework
========================

`Falcon <https://falconframework.org>`__ is a minimalist ASGI/WSGI framework for
building mission-critical REST APIs and microservices, with a focus on
reliability, correctness, and performance at scale.

When it comes to building HTTP APIs, other frameworks weigh you down with tons
of dependencies and unnecessary abstractions. Falcon cuts to the chase with a
clean design that embraces HTTP and the REST architectural style.

Falcon apps work with any `WSGI <https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-3333/>`_
or `ASGI <https://asgi.readthedocs.io/en/latest/>`_ server, and run like a
champ under CPython 3.8+ and PyPy 3.8+.

Quick Links
-----------

* `falconry/user for Falcon users <https://gitter.im/falconry/user>`_ @ Gitter
* `falconry/dev for Falcon contributors <https://gitter.im/falconry/dev>`_ @ Gitter

183	Installation
184	------------
185	
186	PyPy
187	^^^^
188	
189	`PyPy <http://pypy.org/>`__ is the fastest way to run your Falcon app.
190	PyPy3.8+ is supported as of PyPy v7.3.7+.
191	
192	.. code:: bash
193	
194	    $ pip install falcon
195	
196	Or, to install the latest beta or release candidate, if any:
197	
198	.. code:: bash
199	
200	    $ pip install --pre falcon
201	
202	CPython
203	^^^^^^^
204	
205	Falcon also fully supports
206	`CPython <https://www.python.org/downloads/>`__ 3.8+.
207	
208	The latest stable version of Falcon can be installed directly from PyPI:
209	
210	.. code:: bash
211	
212	    $ pip install falcon
213	
214	Or, to install the latest beta or release candidate, if any:
215	
216	.. code:: bash
217	
218	    $ pip install --pre falcon
219	
220	In order to provide an extra speed boost, Falcon automatically compiles itself
221	with `Cython <https://cython.org/>`__ under any
222	`PEP 517 <https://peps.python.org/pep-0517/>`__\-compliant installer.
223	
224	For your convenience, wheels containing pre-compiled binaries are available
225	from PyPI for the majority of common platforms. Even if a binary build for your
226	platform of choice is not available, ``pip`` will pick a pure-Python wheel.
227	You can also cythonize Falcon for your environment; see our
228	`Installation docs <https://falcon.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/install.html>`__.
229	for more information on this and other advanced options.
230	
231	Dependencies
232	^^^^^^^^^^^^
233	
234	Falcon does not require the installation of any other packages.
235	
236	WSGI Server
237	-----------
238	
239	Falcon speaks `WSGI <https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-3333/>`_ (or
240	`ASGI <https://asgi.readthedocs.io/en/latest/>`_; see also below). In order to
241	serve a Falcon app, you will need a WSGI server. Gunicorn and uWSGI are some of
242	the more popular ones out there, but anything that can load a WSGI app will do.
243	
244	.. code:: bash
245	
246	    $ pip install [gunicorn|uwsgi]
247	
248	ASGI Server
249	-----------
250	
251	In order to serve a Falcon ASGI app, you will need an ASGI server. Uvicorn
252	is a popular choice:
253	
254	.. code:: bash
255	
256	    $ pip install uvicorn
257	
258	Source Code
259	-----------
260	
261	Falcon `lives on GitHub <https://github.com/falconry/falcon>`_, making the
262	code easy to browse, download, fork, etc. Pull requests are always welcome! Also,
263	please remember to star the project if it makes you happy. :)
264	
265	Once you have cloned the repo or downloaded a tarball from GitHub, you
266	can install Falcon like this:
267	
268	.. code:: bash
269	
270	    $ cd falcon
271	    $ pip install .
272	
273	Or, if you want to edit the code, first fork the main repo, clone the fork
274	to your desktop, and then run the following to install it using symbolic
275	linking, so that when you change your code, the changes will be automagically
276	available to your app without having to reinstall the package:
277	
278	.. code:: bash
279	
280	    $ cd falcon
281	    $ pip install -e .
282	
283	You can manually test changes to the Falcon framework by switching to the
284	directory of the cloned repo and then running pytest:
285	
286	.. code:: bash
287	
288	    $ cd falcon
289	    $ pip install -r requirements/tests
290	    $ pytest tests
291	
292	Or, to run the default set of tests:
293	
294	.. code:: bash
295	
296	    $ pip install tox && tox
297	
298	See also the `tox.ini <https://github.com/falconry/falcon/blob/master/tox.ini>`_
299	file for a full list of available environments.
300
